summary: Full backend + frontend E2E for the new employee profile-photo feature (Emergent object storage). Added 13 new pytest cases in TestProfilePhoto covering: employee upload of valid PNG/JPEG (200 + photo_file_id returned, /profile reflects id, no storage_path leak), rejection of unsupported types (GIF/text -> 400), rejection of >5 MB uploads (400 with '5 MB' message), owner GET /files/{id} returns image bytes with correct content-type, admin GET /files/{id} for any employee's photo (200), other-employee attempt (403), unauthenticated GET (401), missing file (404), admin POST /profile/photo (403), replaced-photo soft-delete verified via subsequent 404 on old id, and no storage_path/storage_key leakage in /employees or /profile payloads. Full backend suite now 43 passed, 1 skipped (seed employee flag - expected). Also fixed a flaky phone-collision in the session-scoped `new_employee` fixture (time.time()%10000 collided under xdist parallel workers) - replaced with uuid-based unique phones. Frontend Playwright: as Raj (+91 98765 42100 / RajSecure@2026) opened profile panel via header, uploaded a real 1x1 PNG via , saw 'Profile photo updated' toast (success). Logged in as admin (9999999999/Admin@123), employee directory rendered Raj's photo as (naturalWidth=1, complete=true, data-testid='profile-photo-'); other employees without photo showed fallback initials via data-testid='profile-photo-fallback-'. Verified admin activity drawer opens for Raj (shows +91 98765 42100 · Central Market, today totals & collection history). Verified DOM contains NO 'storage_path', 'objstore', 'X-Storage-Key' or 'emergent_key' strings anywhere. Mobile (390x844): scrollWidth=406 vs clientWidth=390 = 16px horizontal overflow on admin dashboard.

minor.issue: Uses requests (sync) inside async endpoint - blocks the event loop for the duration of the object-storage PUT (up to 120s timeout). Should be run in a threadpool (fastapi.concurrency.run_in_threadpool) or migrate to httpx.AsyncClient. Same applies to download_photo in GET /api/files/{id}.
Global `storage_key` cache is never refreshed. If the upstream key expires or rotates, the process will keep sending a stale key until a restart. Consider TTL-based refresh or 401-on-upstream retry.

Magic-bytes / real-image validation is not performed; only content-type header + declared size are checked. A malicious client can send arbitrary bytes with Content-Type: image/png. Server-side sniff (imghdr / PIL.Image.open) is recommended.

Reads full file into memory before size check (`await file.read()` then len). For a 5 MB cap this is fine; for larger caps use streaming size check. Also, file.filename is unused - extension is derived from content-type which is fine.

No Cache-Control header. Browser will re-download on every profile render (ProfilePhoto.jsx already blobs it once per mount, but a private, max-age=300 header would let the frontend cache across re-mounts).

issues: Horizontal overflow of ~16px (scrollWidth 406 vs clientWidth 390). Likely caused by the wide table (Collections feed / expense audit) or the .admin-intro layout. Consider `overflow-x: auto` on `.table-scroll` container or reducing horizontal padding at <=390px breakpoint.

action_items: (Optional but recommended) Wrap storage.upload_profile_photo / download_photo calls in fastapi.concurrency.run_in_threadpool so the event loop is not blocked during multi-second uploads.
(Optional) Add magic-byte validation (imghdr or PIL) in POST /api/profile/photo to defend against Content-Type spoofing.
(Optional) Refresh storage_key on 401/403 from upstream instead of caching for the process lifetime.
Fix mobile horizontal overflow on admin portal at 390px viewport (16px scroll).
critical_code_review_comments: storage.py: sync `requests.put/get` inside async FastAPI endpoints will block the event loop under load. Move to run_in_threadpool or async httpx.
storage.py: `storage_key` global cache with no invalidation is fragile - a single 401 from the upstream storage service will keep failing until pod restart.
router.py upload_own_photo: only trusts the client-declared Content-Type header. Real MIME sniffing would harden this.

router.py: photo_file_id is stored on employee record but there is no DB cleanup for orphaned file records if an employee is deleted; is_deleted flag is only set on replacement, not on employee removal (future concern).

ProfilePhoto.jsx: fetches the blob every time the component mounts (no in-memory cache). Fine for now, but on admin directory with N employees it triggers N parallel authenticated GETs on each render.

success_rate.backend: 100% (43/43 executed, 1 skipped for seed-idempotency by design)
success_rate.frontend: 100% for photo flow (employee upload success toast, admin sees photo, activity drawer works, no secret leakage in DOM)
